messages:
eve_support: FYI — Customer ACME (acct: acme-prod) opened a support ticket: reserved GPU hours dropped ~98h between 2026-03-05 03:00-07:00 UTC but their token usage is flat. Invoice line items show committed hours consumed. Can eng/ops triage?

tony_billing: Thanks, filing here. Invoice snippet: invoice://inv-44321 lineitem: committed_capacity: pool-acme-1: 98.0 GPU-hours, period 2026-03-05T03:00:00Z-2026-03-05T07:00:00Z. Customer says no burst traffic.

sam_sre: Which pool + commit? Any pool-level autoscale/warmup configured for them?

eve_support: pool: pool-acme-1, commit_id: commit-9f3b2, autoscale: on with prewarm probes enabled (default). They say app was idle; only occasional health pings.

alisa_eng: Can you paste the metering query results? I'll run a quick audit. Also, anyone have allocation IDs for that window?

metering-bot: Automated alert: high commit-hours delta detected for account=acme-prod, window=2026-03-05T03:00:00Z..2026-03-05T07:00:00Z. Counted_alloc_events=412, unique_allocs=398, avg_alloc_duration=22s.

tony_billing: That's suspicious — many short allocations. Billing should aggregate to partial-hours, not full hours. Could be double-counting.

alisa_eng: Running internal query now:
```
SELECT alloc_id, start_ts, end_ts, duration_s, pool FROM metering.alloc_events
WHERE pool='pool-acme-1' AND start_ts >= '2026-03-05T03:00:00Z' AND end_ts <= '2026-03-05T07:00:00Z'
ORDER BY start_ts;
```

alisa_eng: Results show ~400 allocations, ~80% are <30s. Many have names like "prewarm-probe-<n>" and alloc_count spikes exactly on the minute boundaries.

sam_sre: Could those be prewarm probes from our health-checker triggering real GPU reservations? We intended probes to be lightweight and not billable.

alisa_eng: Looks like a regression: a change in the probe handler in release v2.14 caused the probe path to call the full reservation API instead of the probe-only endpoint for a subset of configs. That made the scheduler create real allocs (billing-visible) then tear down quickly.

eve_support: Customer confirms they did not flip any config. They saw a flurry of very short allocations in their internal logs too.

alex_sales: Customer is asking for immediate credit + an explanation they can share with finance.

tony_billing: If we confirm the billing pipeline counted each short alloc as 1 hour due to our hourly bucketing bug, we need: 1) estimate excess hours, 2) propose credit, 3) patch and backfill.

alisa_eng: Quick math from events: total_alloc_seconds ~ 141120s -> 39.2 GPU-hours. Billing shows 98h consumed. The difference (~58.8h) is accounted for by our hourly rounding bug where allocations that cross boundary buckets were being counted into multiple hourly buckets because of an off-by-one in bucketization window calculation.

sam_sre: Evidence: several allocs start at 02:59:59.8 and end at 03:00:05.3. Our biller currently maps these to both the 02:00 and 03:00 hourly buckets in edge cases. Should be attributed fractionally to the single hour containing each second.

alisa_eng: Repro steps for devs:
1) Create a short-lived alloc via the dedicated prewarm probe (curl)
2) Observe alloc event in metering service and how it lands in hourly aggregator

Curl example:
```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "X-Prewarm: true" \
  -d '{"pool":"pool-acme-1","probe":true}' https://dedicated.redwood.ai/v1/prewarm
```

alisa_eng: Patch ready to fix bucketization (PR #2034), plus a safe backfill script that recomputes hourly aggregates from raw alloc events for the affected window. Backfill estimate reduces billed hours to ~39.4h for the window.

tony_billing: Proposed customer credit = billed_hours(98.0) - corrected_hours(39.4) = 58.6 GPU-hours. We'll convert to invoice credit at their committed rate. Need approvals from finance.

sam_sre: Short-term mitigation: disable creating real allocs from prewarm probes for pools with "probe_as_alloc":true until patch lands. Can we flip that flag for pool-acme-1?

eve_support: ACME asked for immediate mitigation — please toggle and confirm.

alisa_eng: Toggled probe-as-alloc=false for pool-acme-1 at 2026-03-06T14:22:10Z. No new short allocs since toggle. Also scheduled emergency rollout of PR #2034 to metering (canary then full) — ETA 2 hours.

tony_billing: I'll draft the customer credit note and the finance ticket. Banking on ~58.6 GPU-hour credit.

alex_sales: Customer-facing blurb suggestion: "We identified internal prewarm probe behavior combined with an aggregation bug that caused short-lived reservations to be counted incorrectly on invoices. We have patched the metering system, disabled the probe-to-alloc behavior for your pool, and will issue a credit for the overbilled hours."

sam_sre: Postmortem action items: 1) add alloc-duration-based dedupe to billing pipeline, 2) add unit test for hourly bucketing edge cases, 3) run backfill and verify against invoice generator, 4) alert on >200 short allocs/hour per pool.

eve_support: Thanks all — I've updated the ACME ticket and will share the credit amount once finance confirms. :white_check_mark:
